title: Why Do We Get Goosebumps?
description: Why do we get goosebumps? The simple science of tiny muscles, cold and emotions.
comment: What gives you goosebumps? Music? Fear? Tell me below!

scenes.text: Each hair on your skin has a tiny muscle at its root. When it tightens, the hair stands up.
This happens when you feel cold, scared, or deeply moved by music or a story.
In furry animals, standing hair traps warm air, or makes the animal look bigger.
We have very little hair, so for us it does almost nothing.
Scientists think goosebumps are a leftover from our hairy ancestors.
